science.title: Three-dimensional architecture of the endoplasmic reticulum network in soybean roots reveals extensive remodeling during cyst nematode parasitism
science.description: The soybean cyst nematode Heterodera glycines is a major pathogen of soybean (Glycine max) that induces a specialized feeding structure, the syncytium, in infected roots. The syncytium is the nematode’s sole nutrient source throughout development and contains abundant endoplasmic reticulum (ER). Although cisternal ER (cER) has been described in these feeding sites, the presence and distribution of tubular ER (tER) remain unclear. We investigated the three-dimensional (3D) ultrastructure of the ER in mature H. glycines-induced syncytia using two complementary methods: high-voltage electron tomography (HV-ET) of thick sections fixed and stained with zinc iodide–osmium tetroxide (ZIO), and field-emission scanning electron microscopy (FE-SEM) of osmium-macerated specimens. Three-dimensional reconstructions showed dense tER and cER networks within the examined syncytial regions. Notably, some tER strands were closely associated with and appeared to traverse intercellular openings formed by partial cell-wall dissolution, consistent with local ER continuity between adjacent syncytial compartments. These findings reveal extensive ER remodeling in mature syncytia and provide a structural basis for investigating possible transport functions within the feeding site.

science.title: Integrated technology acceptance model and theory of planned behavior explain anti-osteoporosis medication prescribing among Thai orthopedic surgeons after hip fracture
science.description: A persistent care gap leaves many patients without anti-osteoporosis medications (AOMs) after hip fracture, despite their proven benefit in preventing secondary fractures. We investigated the factors associated with orthopedic surgeons’ intention to prescribe AOMs. A cross-sectional online survey of 264 Thai orthopedic surgeons involved in hip fracture care integrated the technology acceptance model and the theory of planned behavior. Partial least squares structural equation modeling assessed the measurement model’s reliability and validity and tested the hypothesized structural relationships. The integrated model accounted for 63.4% of the variance in prescribing intention. Perceived usefulness of AOMs (β = 0.427; P < 0.001) and subjective norms (β = 0.228; P < 0.001) predicted the surgeons’ attitude toward use. Attitude toward use was the strongest predictor of the intention to prescribe AOMs (β = 0.622; P < 0.001). Self-efficacy did not moderate the attitude–intention relationship but was directly associated with intention (β = 0.201; P = 0.004). These results indicate that prescribing intention is primarily predicted by perceived clinical value and professional norms rather than by procedural simplicity. Interventions to reduce the care gap should therefore emphasize clinical effectiveness, reinforce professional norms, and build surgeons’ self-efficacy through targeted education and training.

science.title: Rare insect discovery reveals a new species from the dinosaur age
science.description: Some 99 million years ago, during the age of the dinosaurs, a tiny insect belonging to a species previously unknown to science became trapped in tree resin. The resin hardened and turned into amber, and the fossil preserved within it has now enabled a team of researchers from the School of Zoology and The Steinhardt Museum of Natural History to identify and describe a new species: Cretodorus noonoo, or "Noo-Noo."

science.title: Retrieval of multiple fibre orientations using X-ray dark-field signal modelling
science.description: Dark-field imaging is widely used to infer fibre orientation from signal modulation as a function of sample orientation. However, current X-ray dark-field retrieval methods are restricted to single orientations and require tomography to resolve overlapping structures. This approach is time-consuming and not suitable for thin materials, which are common in materials science. Here we present, at a proof-of-concept level, a dark-field model capable of retrieving multiple fibre orientations within a single pixel. The model, based on a geometrical description of fibre scattering, was validated through Monte Carlo simulations and experiments using beam-tracking setups with 1D and 2D masks. Results demonstrate orientation retrieval for up to three fibres per pixel, with the 2D mask providing multi-directional sensitivity in a single acquisition and enabling faster and simplified data collection.
